summary: Moving full decode_1 (27.3 us, 6.3x its 4.3 us floor, the only scored decode shape still on FA3) onto master's proven CUDA split-KV kernel with 250 CTA-sized 320-token items is sound and its effect will show up clearly in its own profile row. No rules problem and no companion is needed: the queued chunk640 sibling already serves as the chunk-size A/B.
justification: Plausible. FINDINGS shows full decode_1 at 27.3 us (FA3 main 14.6 + FlashAttnFwdCombine 7.1 + pre 1.3 + norm_gate + gaps) against a 4.3 us floor (20.5 MB of KV). That is the worst ratio to floor of any full shape. At batch 1 the existing kernel with CHUNK 1024 would put only 79 items on the 264 CTA slots, so 60% of SMs would hold one CTA each. At 320 it gets 250 items, one per CTA on about 125 SMs with 2 CTAs each, so roughly 96 KB of ring in flight per SM, comfortably above what Little's law needs at 4.8 TB/s. The template change is safe for TILES = 5: the cross-item meta prefetch needs TILES >= STAGES - 1 = 3 (item k+1's idx/q group is issued at tile k*TILES and must complete before tile (k+1)*TILES is issued at iteration (k+1)*TILES - 3), and that holds. The strided issue_meta loop handles 320 = 256 + 64 correctly. The arithmetic for the expected gain checks out: decode_1 load = 46*13.2 + 16*27.3 µs, so full is 42% of it; -11 to -13 us on full gives about +17% on that load and about +2.7% geomean over 6 loads, which is above the ±1.5% CI floor. The other expected-flat directions follow from the gate (batch > 1 keeps the <1024,4> instantiation byte for byte; verify and sliding sit outside the gate). WEAKEST LINK: the attn-kernel estimate of 7-9 us assumes 2.5-2.9 TB/s, a rate measured at decode_16 where each CTA streams 256 KB+ across items. At batch 1 each CTA streams only 80 KB (5 tiles) behind three dependent cold-DRAM round trips: seqlens read, then cp_wait<0> on page indices, then the first K/V tile. Fixed latency is therefore about 25-35% of the item, and 9-11 us is more realistic. Close behind is the combine: only 16 CTAs, two serial passes over 250 partials (the ml pass is a 128-byte-strided gather), and a second launch gap. The current 4-warp combine already costs 8.2 us at B=16, so 2-3 us here is optimistic and 3-5 us is plausible. Even in that pessimistic case (pre 1.3 + attn 11 + combine 5 + gaps 1.5, about 19 us) the shape still beats 27.3 us, so the direction is robust and only the magnitude is uncertain.
confounders: full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: not a confounder but the substrate. This hypothesis re-instantiates that kernel at a new CHUNK, so any batch-1 weakness of its design (serialized meta prologue, item-end smem merge) is measured together with the chunk choice. The chunk640 sibling, the same code at another chunk, separates the two.

paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: defines the incumbent being replaced (batch 1 unpaired FA3 + sglang rms_norm_gate). The gain therefore also includes dropping FA3's FlashAttnFwdCombine (7.1 us) and the separate norm_gate launch (the epilogue is fused into splitkv_combine), not only the chunk size. That is fine because the hypothesis claims the whole path swap, but the result should not be read as 'chunk 320 is optimal'.

fused-preattention-triton / paired-heads-launch-cleanup: pre-attention kernel and q layout unchanged at batch 1 (PAIRED already false), so they do not confound; the pre kernel's 1.3 us should stay flat and is a sanity check.
sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv: shares the decode_1 load but a different shape and kernel; cold L2 per replay means no cross-shape interaction. Sliding decode_1 must stay at ~13.2 us.
interference: No companion warranted. The readout is per-shape and per-kernel: the profile will show splitkv_attn_kernel<320> and splitkv_combine_kernel<320,16> times directly against FA3 14.6 + combine 7.1. A loss is therefore attributable from the profile (an attn row above about 14 us means the batch-1 prologue/latency design is the problem; a combine row above about 6 us means partial count or combine design is). A gain is unambiguous because the gate isolates one shape and the other 11 shapes act as built-in controls (the batch>1 path is the <1024,4> instantiation of identical code, so decode_16/32 full must be flat within noise or the template refactor itself changed codegen). An ab-revert of any landed hypothesis would not change the interpretation. A chunk-1024-at-batch-1 control would only split path-swap from chunk effect, and the queued sibling full-decode1-cuda-splitkv-chunk640 already gives a second point on that curve. Run chunk320 first: it saturates CTA slots, and the combine cost difference between 250 and 125 partials is small compared with the latency-hiding gain.
rules_flags: None blocking. chunk, max_chunks, grid and workspace shapes derive from config/page_table.shape/SM count only; no host syncs; every key is attended (positions < cache_seqlens masked only past the length); Q rounded to FP8 E4M3 (allowed), P packed to f16 in [0,1] as on the landed path; KV stays FP8.

Practical: the 16 pre-timing tests contain no batch-1 full decode case (the only batch-1 full test is q_len 8, outside the gate), so the new path first meets the judge at timing; correctness rests on the import-time self-check, which must include the [80000] and [5000] batch-1 cases at grid 3 (exercises TILES=5 cross-item meta double-buffering) as specified. The self-check must fail closed (disable _EXT) as today.
Compile-time: renaming the module forces a fresh build of two instantiations of each kernel; keep an eye on the 15-minute run budget (low risk).
open_questions: Does the combine's first pass (ml max over 250 partials, 128-byte strided reads) plus the 512-thread single-CTA-per-head design actually come in under 3 us? If not, the follow-up is a combine that reads ml once (online merge in one pass) or a one-launch tail merge in the attn kernel.
Would prefetching item 0's page indices before the seqlens prefix sum (B=1 needs no prefix) remove one dependent DRAM round trip, worth roughly 0.5-1 us at batch 1?

Merge risk: full-verify-cuda-streamk-splitkv and full-verify1-cuda-streamk-batch1 (running/queued) likely edit _SPLITKV_CUDA too; the CHUNK template refactor will conflict textually with them if both land.
At 250 items on 264 slots, 14 CTAs exit immediately and ~7 SMs host one CTA; does SM-level imbalance (some SMs 2 CTAs, some 1) show up as a tail? Chunk 304-ish (264 items) is a possible later tune.
